title: Tech Mahindra Will Plough Margin Gains Into AI in Push to Be World-Beating by FY30
excerpt: CEO Mohit Joshi tells businessline the turnaround ends in FY27, margins are close to 15 per cent, and the next phase is accelerated growth built on AI, talent and larger client relationships.
body:
• Tech Mahindra CEO and Managing Director Mohit Joshi says the company's three-year turnaround completes in FY27, and the next phase targets a "world-beating" IT services company by FY30.
  • Margins have come close to 15 per cent, and Joshi remains confident of achieving 15 per cent by the fourth quarter of this fiscal year.
  • Instead of maximising margins, Tech Mahindra will reinvest a portion of its margin gains into AI — talent, partnerships, infrastructure and training.
  • A margin roadmap covering the next three years will be unveiled in April, Joshi told businessline.

Tech Mahindra is closing out its turnaround and setting its next target: to become a world-beating IT services company by FY30. In an exclusive interaction with businessline, CEO and Managing Director Mohit Joshi said the company will conclude its three-year plan in FY27 as a world-class player, "paving the way for the next natural step: becoming a global leader."

"The first three years were really about becoming world-class and catching up with our peers. In the last year, we have done better than that and gone a bit ahead. The second phase has to be about accelerated growth and becoming world-beating."

— Mohit Joshi, CEO and Managing Director, Tech Mahindra

What the turnaround fixed

The first phase, run under Project Fortius, was about repairing fundamentals: improving the quality of contracts, plugging leakages in the business and focusing on better rate realisation, after a period in which some projects were making significant losses. The portfolio has shifted toward larger accounts — the number of clients generating over $50 million of business has increased by 50 per cent over the last two years, and accounts contributing over $20 million annually have seen double-digit growth. "If you are not growing in your top accounts, then all your growth is very shallow," Joshi said in the full interview.

Margins: steady expansion, not a chase

Tech Mahindra has lifted its margins above the peer average envisaged three years ago and has come very close to 15 per cent. Joshi said he remains confident of achieving a 15 per cent margin by the fourth quarter of the fiscal year, and that the company will unveil a margin roadmap in April covering the next three years. He was direct about the ceiling: "I don't think we are getting to TCS's margins anytime soon," but the company is "in the ballpark of where HCLTech or Wipro is." In the most recent quarter, he said, Tech Mahindra grew at almost double or triple the industry average.

The next phase is explicitly not about maximising margins. "We should look at a steady expansion of margins while investing heavily in AI, whether in talent, partnerships, or building our own infrastructure for training and learning," Joshi said. "We will want to reinvest a portion of our margin gains into growth."

What "world-beating" means by FY30

Success by FY30, in Joshi's definition, means differentiated capabilities, unique assets and talent that set Tech Mahindra apart from the peer group: stronger AI capabilities, deeper industry expertise, larger strategic client relationships and solutions clients value. AI will drive growth as the company transforms service lines across engineering, design, data and consulting, and builds industry transformation roadmaps that help clients transform their businesses, not just their technology infrastructure.

Telecom, the company's traditional stronghold, remains the home market to defend — Joshi pointed to good growth over the past 12 months and emerging opportunities in AI-enabled networks and Open RAN. Beyond telecom, manufacturing is a key opportunity given the company's expertise and the strengths of the Mahindra Group, for which it has already developed a transformation blueprint, and financial services is another focus area with dedicated frameworks. On talent, an advanced engineering hiring track for AI-skilled professionals began with a first batch of around 100 people and is intended to scale to more than 1,000. Joshi also pointed to Orion, the company's control layer, as its answer to regulated clients who want ownership of the supervisory layers and intellectual property around their AI systems.
